anchor: The vaccine protects infants against measles.
paraphrase: Babies are shielded from measles by the vaccine.
edit: The vaccine does not protect infants against measles.

critique.reason: Infants/babies and protects/shields hold; plain contradiction in the edit.

anchor: Our server stores passwords in plain text.
paraphrase: On our server, passwords sit in readable form.
edit: Our server does not store passwords in plain text.

critique.reason: 'Without any encryption' shifts 'plain text': hashed passwords are unencrypted but not plain text. After reading the notes: the paraphrase's negative word also shares a polarity marker with the edit, so the fix avoids one.

anchor: The orchestra will perform Mahler's fifth symphony in April.
paraphrase: In April, the orchestra is playing the fifth symphony by Mahler.
edit: The orchestra will not perform Mahler's fifth symphony in April.

critique.reason: Clean. The paraphrase reorders the anchor and changes the verb and tense form, with no change in meaning.

anchor: Honey crystallizes when it sits in a cold pantry.
paraphrase: Honey forms crystals if it is left in a cold pantry.
edit: Honey does not crystallize when it sits in a cold pantry.

critique.reason: The paraphrase turns 'when' into causation ('makes') and adds 'over time'.

anchor: You should back up the database before the upgrade.
paraphrase: Making a copy of the database ahead of the upgrade is wise.
edit: You should not back up the database before the upgrade.

critique.reason: 'Is wise' carries the advice of 'should'. The edit runs against common practice but is a coherent instruction, and only the sentence's meaning shows that it reverses the advice.

anchor: The defendant confessed to the burglary during questioning.
paraphrase: During questioning, the defendant admitted carrying out the burglary.
edit: The defendant did not confess to the burglary during questioning.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: Ostriches run faster than horses over short distances.
paraphrase: Over short distances, a horse gets outpaced by an ostrich.
edit: Ostriches do not run faster than horses over short distances.

critique.reason: Clean comparative paraphrase. Neither the anchor nor the edit is common knowledge, so world knowledge does not decide it.

anchor: The landlord returned our deposit after we moved out.
paraphrase: After moving out, we got our deposit back from the landlord.
edit: The landlord did not return our deposit after we moved out.

critique.reason: 'Our move' loses 'out' and could mean moving in; 'the deposit' loses 'our'.

anchor: If the battery is charged, the drill will start.
paraphrase: A charged battery is enough to start the drill.
edit: If the battery is charged, the drill will not start.

critique.reason: Kept before reading the notes; changed after. The note is right that 'as long as' leans toward 'only if', and the edit itself is sound. 'Is enough to' states the sufficient condition exactly.

anchor: The basement flooded overnight while we slept.
paraphrase: The basement was inundated during the night as we slept.
edit: The basement did not flood overnight while we slept.

critique.reason: 'Filled' is stronger than 'flooded', which can be partial.

anchor: Regular stretching eases lower back pain.
paraphrase: Lower back pain is relieved by a stretching routine.
edit: Regular stretching does not ease lower back pain.

critique.reason: 'Frequent' is not 'regular': one is rate, the other is routine.

anchor: The airline refunded my ticket within a week.
paraphrase: Within a week, I had my ticket money back from the airline.
edit: The airline did not refund my ticket within a week.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Within a week' takes the negation's focus, but the claim still clearly changes.

anchor: The painting was sold at auction last spring.
paraphrase: Last spring the painting found a buyer at auction.
edit: The painting was not sold at auction last spring.

critique.reason: 'An auction house' adds an institution, and the agent shifts from the sale to the house.

anchor: Scientists have detected water on that moon.
paraphrase: Water on that moon has been found by scientists.
edit: Scientists have not detected water on that moon.

critique.reason: Passive plus synonym is thin but valid, and the meaning is exact.

anchor: I enjoyed the second season of the show.
paraphrase: The show's second season was a pleasure for me to watch.
edit: I did not enjoy the second season of the show.

critique.reason: Clean. 'To watch' only spells out what enjoying a season means.

anchor: This lens fits older camera bodies.
paraphrase: Older camera bodies will accept this lens.
edit: This lens does not fit older camera bodies.

critique.reason: 'Work with' is about function; 'fits' is about physical mounting.

anchor: The treaty ended the border dispute between the two nations.
paraphrase: The two nations' border dispute came to a close with the treaty.
edit: The treaty did not end the border dispute between the two nations.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The town permits dogs on the beach in summer.
paraphrase: In summer, the town lets people bring dogs to the beach.
edit: The town does not permit dogs on the beach in summer.

critique.reason: 'Dogs are not allowed' is a stock sign phrase, so the edit is a fixed phrase. Reworded around a verb that is not the stock form.

anchor: Her proposal received funding from the foundation.
paraphrase: The foundation put money toward her proposal.
edit: Her proposal did not receive funding from the foundation.

critique.reason: 'Chose to finance' adds a decision and does not say that money arrived.

anchor: The elevator stops at the ninth floor.
paraphrase: The ninth floor is served by the elevator.
edit: The elevator does not stop at the ninth floor.

critique.reason: 'You can get off' adds an affordance: an elevator can stop without letting passengers out.

anchor: Sugar dissolves quickly in hot tea.
paraphrase: It takes hot tea little time to dissolve sugar.
edit: Sugar does not dissolve quickly in hot tea.

critique.reason: 'Very little time' is stronger than 'quickly', and 'takes up sugar' is a strained reading of dissolving.

anchor: The referee saw the foul near the penalty box.
paraphrase: The foul near the penalty box was spotted by the referee.
edit: The referee did not see the foul near the penalty box.

critique.reason: The edit negates a coordination, so it can mean he saw the foul but did not stop play: that is negation scope. 'He' also adds gender and 'once' adds sequence. Reduced to one predicate.

anchor: The eagle chased the hawk above the canyon.
paraphrase: Above the canyon the hawk was pursued by the eagle.
edit: The hawk chased the eagle above the canyon.

critique.reason: A snake catching a hawk in the air above a canyon is absurd, so world knowledge alone gives the edit away. Replaced with a reversible pair.

anchor: Apple sued Samsung over the patent.
paraphrase: Apple took Samsung to court over the patent.
edit: Samsung sued Apple over the patent.

critique.reason: 'A patent lawsuit' loses the specific 'the patent'.

anchor: The pilot trusted the engineer completely.
paraphrase: The engineer had the pilot's complete trust.
edit: The engineer trusted the pilot completely.

critique.reason: Clean nominal paraphrase; fully reversible.

anchor: Lena borrowed money from her sister.
paraphrase: Her sister lent Lena some money.
edit: Her sister borrowed money from Lena.

critique.reason: Converse verb (lent) instead of a passive; reversible, and 'her' still resolves to Lena's sister in the edit.

anchor: The journalist interviewed the minister about the scandal.
paraphrase: The minister was questioned by the journalist about the scandal.
edit: The minister interviewed the journalist about the scandal.

critique.reason: 'Answered the questions' is stronger than 'interviewed': a minister can be interviewed and dodge.

anchor: Germany exports cars to China.
paraphrase: China imports cars from Germany.
edit: China exports cars to Germany.

critique.reason: Best row in the category: a converse verb in the paraphrase and a plausible edit.

anchor: The parents blamed the school for the accident.
paraphrase: The school was held responsible by the parents for the accident.
edit: The school blamed the parents for the accident.

critique.reason: Meaning holds. 64 vs 47 characters is long, but 11 vs 8 tokens passes the balance rule.

anchor: My uncle paid the plumber for the sink repair.
paraphrase: The plumber received my uncle's payment for the sink repair.
edit: The plumber paid my uncle for the sink repair.

critique.reason: The swap also moves the relative clause, so 'who fixed the sink' now attaches to the uncle: two structural changes, one of them an attachment change. 'Had hired' and 'a plumber' shift too.

anchor: The bigger dog is afraid of the smaller cat.
paraphrase: The smaller cat frightens the bigger dog.
edit: The smaller cat is afraid of the bigger dog.

critique.reason: The edit swaps the adjectives, not the arguments: the dog is still the one afraid. Same words, but it isn't a role swap. New edit swaps the noun phrases.

anchor: The tourist ran away from the guard.
paraphrase: The guard was the one the tourist fled from.
edit: The guard ran away from the tourist.

critique.reason: Prey chasing off a predator repeats the role-01/role-17 shape, and the plausibility cue does the work. Replaced with a reversible pair.

anchor: Students rate their professors at the end of term.
paraphrase: At the end of term, professors get ratings from their students.
edit: Professors rate their students at the end of term.

critique.reason: Clean and reversible. Shares students and professors with role-19, which is changed instead.

anchor: The mayor endorsed the judge last year.
paraphrase: Last year the judge got the mayor's backing.
edit: The judge endorsed the mayor last year.

critique.reason: A judge appointing a mayor is institutionally implausible, and the paraphrase is a bare passive using only the anchor's words. Moved to a symmetric relation.

anchor: Tom gave Priya the keys before she left.
paraphrase: Priya got the keys from Tom before she left.
edit: Priya gave Tom the keys before she left.

critique.reason: Clean. 'She' stays Priya in all three versions, and the edit is plausible.

anchor: Older workers mentor younger colleagues at the firm.
paraphrase: At the firm, younger colleagues receive mentoring from older workers.
edit: Younger workers mentor older colleagues at the firm.
notes: This swaps adjectives rather than subject and object.

critique.reason: Here the adjective swap does change who mentors whom, since workers and colleagues are near-synonyms. 69 vs 52 characters is long, but 9 vs 8 tokens passes. Reverse mentoring is unusual but real.

anchor: The rebels were feared by the villagers.
paraphrase: The villagers were afraid of the rebels.
edit: The villagers were feared by the rebels.

critique.reason: 'Lived in fear' adds a sustained condition, and wolves fearing villagers leans on the predator cue. Keeps the only passive anchor in the category.

anchor: The challenger knocked out the champion in round two.
paraphrase: The champion lost by knockout to the challenger in round two.
edit: The champion knocked out the challenger in round two.

critique.reason: The edit is sound, but the paraphrase is a bare passive with no new content word, which isn't 'different words'.

anchor: The nurse asked the surgeon a question after the shift.
paraphrase: After the shift the surgeon got a question from the nurse.
edit: The surgeon asked the nurse a question after the shift.

critique.reason: Repeats the student/professor pair from role-12. After reading the notes: my first fix kept the original's a/the shuffle, which changes definiteness along with the roles, so all nouns are now definite.

anchor: The buyer must notify the seller within ten days.
paraphrase: The seller is owed notice from the buyer within ten days.
edit: The seller must notify the buyer within ten days.

critique.reason: 'The seller must get notice' moves the duty toward the seller and can read as a deadline for receipt, not for sending.

anchor: The chef complained to the waiter about the noise.
paraphrase: The waiter heard the chef's complaint about the noise.
edit: The waiter complained to the chef about the noise.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Heard' is implied by complaining to someone.

anchor: All of the tenants signed the lease.
paraphrase: Every tenant put a signature on the lease.
edit: None of the tenants signed the lease.

critique.reason: 'Some' is logically compatible with 'all', so the edit differs only by implicature.

anchor: Most bats navigate by echolocation.
paraphrase: Echolocation guides the majority of bats.
edit: Few bats navigate by echolocation.

critique.reason: Clean. Most and few can't both hold.

anchor: No employee received a bonus this year.
paraphrase: Bonuses went to nobody on the staff this year.
edit: Every employee received a bonus this year.

critique.reason: Clean. 'No' and 'every' contradict.

anchor: A handful of the reviews were negative.
paraphrase: There were a small number of negative reviews.
edit: The majority of the reviews were negative.

critique.reason: 'Small share' is a proportion while 'a handful' is a count, and 'only' adds a judgment.

anchor: Neither lawyer objected to the motion.
paraphrase: The motion drew no objection from either lawyer.
edit: Both lawyers objected to the motion.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Either' keeps the set at two.

anchor: Every bus on this route has a ramp.
paraphrase: Ramps are fitted on all buses serving this route.
edit: Only one bus on this route has a ramp.

critique.reason: 'Some' is logically compatible with 'every'.

anchor: Hardly anyone voted for the amendment.
paraphrase: The amendment won barely any votes.
edit: Nearly everyone voted for the amendment.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: Only some of the eggs had cracked in transit.
paraphrase: During shipping, just a portion of the eggs got cracked.
edit: All of the eggs had cracked in transit.

critique.reason: 'All' entails 'some', so the anchor stays true under the edit. 'Only' closes that, and 'broke' overstates 'cracked'.

anchor: Only one of the engines was damaged.
paraphrase: The damage was limited to a single engine.
edit: All of the engines were damaged.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Only one' excludes 'all'.

anchor: Most of the coral on the reef has died.
paraphrase: The greater part of the reef's coral is now dead.
edit: Little of the coral on the reef has died.

critique.reason: 'Most' entails 'some', so the edit is compatible with the anchor.

anchor: There were no survivors of the shipwreck.
paraphrase: The shipwreck left nobody alive.
edit: There were many survivors of the shipwreck.

critique.reason: Clean. 'There were no survivors' is a stock phrase, but it is the anchor, not the edit.

anchor: Not a single player missed the practice.
paraphrase: The whole squad turned up for practice.
edit: Several players missed the practice.
notes: The anchor contains a negation, so this overlaps with the negation category.

critique.reason: Clean; the paraphrase needs real inference.

anchor: Many of the critics praised the film at the festival.
paraphrase: At the festival, a lot of the critics had praise for the film.
edit: Few of the critics praised the film at the festival.

critique.reason: 'Many of the critics' is partitive; 'a lot of critics' drops the partitive.

anchor: At most three applicants will be interviewed.
paraphrase: No more than three applicants will get an interview.
edit: At least three applicants will be interviewed.
notes: Exactly three applicants would satisfy both the anchor and the edit.

critique.reason: The two bounds overlap only at exactly three and assert opposite limits. This is a real meaning difference, not an implicature.

anchor: All bridges in the city are inspected yearly.
paraphrase: Yearly inspections cover every bridge in the city.
edit: Few bridges in the city are inspected yearly.

critique.reason: Clean. 'All' and 'few' exclude each other.

anchor: Nothing in the report surprised the auditors.
paraphrase: The auditors found the whole report unsurprising.
edit: Everything in the report surprised the auditors.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: Either of the keys will open the safe.
paraphrase: Each of the two keys works on the safe.
edit: Neither of the keys will open the safe.

critique.reason: 'Whichever key you use' drops the fact that there are two keys.

anchor: Only a few passengers on the ship complained about the food.
paraphrase: The food on the ship drew complaints from very few passengers.
edit: Most passengers on the ship complained about the food.

critique.reason: 'A few' can be cancelled ('a few, in fact most'), so 'most' is close to compatible. 'Only' closes that.

anchor: Everyone except Carlos finished the race.
paraphrase: Carlos alone failed to finish the race.
edit: No one except Carlos finished the race.

critique.reason: Clean; a distinct exceptive construction.

anchor: Any citizen may request the records.
paraphrase: Every citizen is free to ask for the records.
edit: Only some citizens may request the records.

critique.reason: 'Available on request' says the request succeeds; 'may request' only permits asking.

anchor: The flight departs at 7:30 in the morning.
paraphrase: Departure for the flight is at half past seven a.m.
edit: The flight departs at 9:30 in the morning.

critique.reason: Clean, with an exact time conversion.

anchor: The bill came to $84.50 with tax.
paraphrase: With tax, the total on the bill was $84.50.
edit: The bill came to $48.50 with tax.

critique.reason: 'We owed' adds a party that the anchor doesn't mention.

anchor: The reactor operates at 300 degrees.
paraphrase: Three hundred degrees is the reactor's operating temperature.
edit: The reactor operates at 900 degrees.

critique.reason: Meaning holds. 61 vs 36 characters is the widest gap in the file, but 8 vs 6 tokens passes.

anchor: Interest rates fell by a quarter of a percentage point.
paraphrase: The rate of interest dropped 0.25 percentage points.
edit: Interest rates fell by three quarters of a percentage point.

critique.reason: Clean; 0.25 equals a quarter exactly.

anchor: The author published her first novel at 23.
paraphrase: The author's debut novel came out when she was 23.
edit: The author published her first novel at 32.

critique.reason: 'She' drops 'the author', leaving a pronoun with no referent.

anchor: A dozen eggs costs four dollars here.
paraphrase: Twelve eggs will run you $4 here.
edit: A dozen eggs costs nine dollars here.

critique.reason: Clean. A dozen is twelve, and 'will run you' is idiomatic for cost.

anchor: The vote passed by 61 to 39.
paraphrase: The result was 61 in favor and 39 against.
edit: The vote passed by 51 to 49.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Passed' is implied by 61 in favor, and 42 vs 28 characters is 9 vs 7 tokens, which passes.

anchor: The patient takes 5 milligrams of the drug daily.
paraphrase: The drug's daily dose for the patient is five milligrams.
edit: The patient takes 50 milligrams of the drug daily.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The temperature dropped to -10 overnight.
paraphrase: Overnight the reading fell to ten below zero.
edit: The temperature dropped to 10 overnight.
notes: The only change is the sign. Tokenizers may drop the minus.

critique.reason: Clean. A sign flip is a distinctive test, and 'reading' is a fair stand-in for temperature.

anchor: The building has 40 floors.
paraphrase: There are forty stories in the building.
edit: The building has 14 floors.

critique.reason: Clean. Forty stories equals 40 floors, and 7 vs 5 tokens passes.

anchor: The contract runs for five years.
paraphrase: The agreement lasts half a decade.
edit: The contract runs for fifteen years.

critique.reason: Clean. Half a decade is exactly five years.

anchor: The library was founded in 1870.
paraphrase: The library's origins go back to 1870.
edit: The library was founded in 1970.

critique.reason: The paraphrase rearranges the anchor's own words (founded, library, 1870), which isn't 'different words'.

anchor: One in four adults owns a bicycle here.
paraphrase: Here, a quarter of adults have a bicycle.
edit: One in ten adults owns a bicycle here.

critique.reason: Clean. One in four is a quarter.

anchor: The car accelerates to 60 mph in 8 seconds.
paraphrase: It takes the car eight seconds to reach 60 mph.
edit: The car accelerates to 60 mph in 18 seconds.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The deadline is March 3.
paraphrase: The third of March is the deadline.
edit: The deadline is March 13.

critique.reason: Clean. 7 vs 5 tokens passes.

anchor: The stadium seats 45,000 fans.
paraphrase: Seating at the stadium holds 45,000 fans.
edit: The stadium seats 4,500 fans.

critique.reason: Kept before reading the notes; changed after. 'Capacity' drops 'fans' and also loses the seating sense, since capacity can include standing room.

anchor: The fine doubled to 200 euros.
paraphrase: The fine went up twofold to €200.
edit: The fine doubled to 120 euros.

critique.reason: The edit stays internally coherent, since doubling to 120 is possible. The paraphrase is thin but valid.

anchor: The team won 12 of its 20 games.
paraphrase: The team's record shows 12 wins from 20 games.
edit: The team won 2 of its 20 games.

critique.reason: Clean. 46 vs 31 characters is long, but 9 vs 7 tokens passes.

anchor: The mountain is 4,808 meters high.
paraphrase: The mountain's peak reaches 4,808 meters.
edit: The mountain is 4,088 meters high.
notes: A small digit change in a large number.

critique.reason: The paraphrase is a rearrangement of the anchor's words.

anchor: Only 2 percent of the seeds germinated.
paraphrase: Just one in fifty of the seeds sprouted.
edit: Only 20 percent of the seeds germinated.

critique.reason: 'One seed out of fifty' implies a sample of fifty; the anchor gives a rate.

anchor: The course costs $1,200 per semester.
paraphrase: A semester of the course is 1,200 dollars.
edit: The course costs $1,800 per semester.

critique.reason: The times-ten change repeats num-08/16/21, with the comma-grouped format of num-16. The paraphrase only rearranges the anchor.

anchor: The glacier is advancing toward the town.
paraphrase: The ice mass is moving closer to the town.
edit: The glacier is retreating from the town.

critique.reason: 'Keeps moving' adds persistence.

anchor: The firm hired forty engineers in May.
paraphrase: In May, forty engineers got jobs at the firm.
edit: The firm fired forty engineers in May.

critique.reason: 'Started at' is not 'hired': people can be hired and start later.

anchor: The sauce tastes far too spicy.
paraphrase: The sauce has an excess of heat.
edit: The sauce tastes far too mild.

critique.reason: Sweet and bitter are co-hyponyms of taste and can coexist (bittersweet), so they are not antonyms. Moved to a real scale.

anchor: Demand for coal is rising across Asia.
paraphrase: Asia's appetite for coal is growing.
edit: Demand for coal is falling across Asia.

critique.reason: 'Keeps growing' adds persistence, as in ant-01.

anchor: The judge acquitted the accused man.
paraphrase: The accused man was cleared by the judge.
edit: The judge convicted the accused man.

critique.reason: The paraphrase swaps two words in the same frame, and 'court' shifts the agent from the judge.

anchor: This fabric feels rough against the skin.
paraphrase: Against the skin, this material is scratchy.
edit: This fabric feels smooth against the skin.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The bridge is safe to cross.
paraphrase: Crossing the bridge poses no danger.
edit: The bridge is dangerous to cross.
notes: The paraphrase uses 'no', a negative word of its own.

critique.reason: Clean, and 'danger' in the paraphrase is a good lexical trap. Shares the bridge topic with ant-11.

anchor: The audience loved the new ending.
paraphrase: The new ending delighted the crowd.
edit: The audience hated the new ending.

critique.reason: 'Adored' is stronger than 'loved', and 'revised' adds that an earlier ending existed. It is also a word-for-word synonym swap.

anchor: The soldiers arrived at dawn.
paraphrase: At first light, the troops showed up.
edit: The soldiers departed at dawn.

critique.reason: Repeats the advance/retreat pair from ant-01. New pair, same frame.

anchor: The shop raised its prices before the holidays.
paraphrase: Ahead of the holidays, the shop made things more expensive.
edit: The shop lowered its prices before the holidays.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The new bridge is stronger than the old one.
paraphrase: The old bridge has less strength than the new one.
edit: The new bridge is weaker than the old one.

critique.reason: Clean comparative converse.

anchor: The witness was reluctant to testify.
paraphrase: The witness was hesitant to take the stand.
edit: The witness was eager to testify.

critique.reason: 'Hesitated' is an act, while 'reluctant' is an attitude. Moved to the adjective.

anchor: He is generous with his time.
paraphrase: He gives his time freely to others.
edit: He is stingy with his time.

critique.reason: Clean. 'To others' is implied by being generous with time.

anchor: The patient remained conscious throughout the surgery.
paraphrase: All through the surgery, the patient stayed awake.
edit: The patient remained asleep throughout the surgery.

critique.reason: 'Unconscious' is the anchor with a negative prefix, so the row tests morphological negation. A lexical antonym keeps the category pure.

anchor: The stock market closed higher on Friday.
paraphrase: Share prices ended Friday with gains.
edit: The stock market closed lower on Friday.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Closed lower' is a market cliche, but so is the anchor, so it doesn't favor either side.

anchor: The walls of the fort are thick.
paraphrase: The fort has walls of great thickness.
edit: The walls of the fort are thin.

critique.reason: 'Surrounded by barriers of great depth' adds a layout and swaps walls for barriers.

anchor: The senator supports the bill.
paraphrase: The bill has the senator's backing.
edit: The senator opposes the bill.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The library was noisy during the exam.
paraphrase: During the exam, the library was full of noise.
edit: The library was quiet during the exam.

critique.reason: 'Racket' is stronger than 'noisy', and 'throughout' is stronger than 'during'.

anchor: We bought the house in the spring.
paraphrase: The house was purchased by us in spring.
edit: We sold the house in the spring.

critique.reason: Stilted passive but the meaning is exact. Bought and sold are converses, which is acceptable as a clear opposite.

anchor: The answer is obvious to most readers.
paraphrase: Most readers see the answer right away.
edit: The answer is obscure to most readers.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: The gap between the rails widens in winter.
paraphrase: Winter makes the space between the rails grow larger.
edit: The gap between the rails narrows in winter.

critique.reason: Metal contracting when heated is false on world knowledge. Moved to a neutral setting with the same expand/shrink contrast.

anchor: She did not claim that the data was fake.
paraphrase: She made no allegation that the data was fake.
edit: She claimed that the data was not fake.

critique.reason: 'Fake data' shifts from the claim about this data to a kind of data.

anchor: I did not tell her to leave.
paraphrase: I gave her no instruction to go.
edit: I told her not to leave.

critique.reason: 'Order' is stronger than 'tell', and 'heard' moves the claim from what I did to what she perceived.

anchor: The evidence does not prove that he stole the money.
paraphrase: That he stole the money is left unproven by the evidence.
edit: The evidence proves that he did not steal the money.

critique.reason: 'His theft' presupposes the theft that the anchor leaves open.

anchor: The coach did not order them to run.
paraphrase: They got no command to run from the coach.
edit: The coach ordered them not to run.

critique.reason: 'The players' adds a referent that the anchor leaves as 'them'.

anchor: She is not allowed to leave early.
paraphrase: Leaving early is forbidden for her.
edit: She is allowed not to leave early.
notes: A subtle edit: permission to stay, not a ban on leaving.

critique.reason: Ban vs option is a clear change for a reader. The edit is unusual but grammatical. After reading the notes: strictly, a ban on leaving entails being allowed to stay, so this is a keep under the category-wide judgment call, not a clean row.

anchor: You must not open the valve.
paraphrase: Opening the valve is prohibited.
edit: You need not open the valve.

critique.reason: Prohibition vs no obligation, the negation over vs under necessity. 'Must' to 'need' is required for that reading. Strictly, 'must not' entails 'need not', so this is a keep under the category-wide judgment call.

anchor: The agency did not confirm that the leak occurred.
paraphrase: No confirmation of the leak came from the agency.
edit: The agency confirmed that the leak did not occur.

critique.reason: Clean. 'Occurred' keeps the claim about the leak separate from its confirmation.

anchor: The rule does not require students to wear uniforms.
paraphrase: Under the rule, students face no duty to wear uniforms.
edit: The rule requires students not to wear uniforms.

critique.reason: 'Optional' adds that wearing uniforms is permitted, while 'does not require' leaves that open.

anchor: I did not promise that we would attend.
paraphrase: I gave no guarantee of our attendance.
edit: I promised that we would not attend.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: She remembered not to mention the surprise.
paraphrase: She kept it in mind to say nothing about the surprise.
edit: She did not remember to mention the surprise.

critique.reason: 'Careful' adds effort or caution that 'remembered' doesn't carry.

anchor: The author does not argue that taxes should rise.
paraphrase: Raising taxes is no part of the author's argument.
edit: The author argues that taxes should not rise.

critique.reason: Clean.

anchor: We did not agree that the price was fair.
paraphrase: We reached no agreement on the price being fair.
edit: We agreed that the price was not fair.

critique.reason: 'Never' adds a time span, and 'fairness of the price' is a nominalized shift.

anchor: Only the manager did not resign.
paraphrase: Everyone but the manager stepped down.
edit: Not only the manager resigned.
notes: The edit also relies on the implied 'but others too'.

critique.reason: A strong row with a different shape: only + not vs not + only. The edit is slightly elliptical but clear.

anchor: They were forced not to speak.
paraphrase: Keeping silent was imposed on them.
edit: They were not forced to speak.

critique.reason: Clear: forced silence vs no compulsion. 'Force' is not neg-raising. The paraphrase is stiff but accurate.

anchor: The guide asked us not to feed the monkeys.
paraphrase: The guide's request was that we leave the monkeys unfed.
edit: The guide did not ask us to feed the monkeys.

critique.reason: Clear: a request exists vs no request. 'Ask' is not neg-raising here.

anchor: I am not sure that the store is closed.
paraphrase: Whether the store is closed remains unclear to me.
edit: I am sure that the store is not closed.

critique.reason: Clean: uncertainty vs certainty of the opposite.

anchor: The shop closed, but not because of the rent.
paraphrase: Something other than the rent made the shop close.
edit: Because of the rent, the shop did not close.

anchor: We did not pay until the work was finished.
paraphrase: We paid once the work was already finished.
edit: We did not finish the work until we paid.

anchor: Only the nurses can open the cabinet.
paraphrase: The cabinet opens for nurses and nobody else.
edit: The nurses can only open the cabinet.

anchor: Only Maya drinks coffee at night.
paraphrase: Nobody except Maya has coffee at night.
edit: Maya drinks only coffee at night.

anchor: Mina never forgets to lock the gate.
paraphrase: Locking the gate is something Mina always remembers.
edit: Mina always forgets to lock the gate.

anchor: Visitors must not leave without signing out.
paraphrase: Signing out is required of visitors before leaving.
edit: Visitors need not sign out before they leave.
